steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Evaluation = analysis + judgement. You must say HOW effective something was AND WHY.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Criteria for evaluation: did the choice serve the production's intention? Did it communicate meaning clearly? Did it engage the audience?

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Support every judgement with SPECIFIC evidence from the production — never make unsupported claims.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Performance evaluation: vocal skills, physical skills, characterisation, interaction. Design evaluation: set, costume, lighting, sound, props.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: What criteria would you use to evaluate whether a performer's choices were effective? | How would you evaluate a lighting design's contribution to a production? Give specific examples. | Explain the difference between analysis and evaluation. Why does evaluation require judgement?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Did the performer serve the character's truth? Were vocal and physical choices precise and consistent? Did they interact authentically with others? Did their choices serve the production's intention?  | Describe the lighting design (colour, intensity, direction, movement); explain what each choice connoted; evaluate whether it served the production's intention; judge its effectiveness on the audience | Analysis identifies WHAT was done and HOW it created meaning. Evaluation adds a JUDGEMENT about effectiveness. Analysis: 'The designer used red lighting.' Evaluation: 'The designer's use of red lighti

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Evaluation REQUIRES judgement — you must say whether it was effective and why Support every judgement with a specific moment from the production Effectiveness = did it serve the INTENTION? Not just 'was it impressive?' Be balanced — acknowledge both strengths and areas for improvement
